record.original_question: Fix a class C of matrices and let C_n denote the subclass of matrices in C of order at most n. What is the largest integer n for which every matrix in C_n is positive stable? The paper identifies the following classes as especially relevant: (i) the matrices A_{n,k,t} for positive integers n and k and for t ∈ (0,1), (ii) GKK τ-matrices, (iii) GKK matrices, and (iv) τ-matrices.

evidence.quote: For various classes C of matrices, this raises the following three questions concerning the subclass Cn of all matrices in C of order less than or equal to n.
3a. What is the maximum n such that all matrices in class Cn are stable?

Speciﬁc classes C of interest include i. The class of matrices An,k,t for positive integers n and k, and for t ∈ (0, 1), ii. The class of GKK τ -matrices, iii. The class of GKK matrices, iv. The class of τ -matrices.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as an open problem in the open-problems list on GKK τ-matrices. A subsequent paper "Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable" exhibits unstable examples, showing the threshold is finite, but no source identifies the exact maximum order n for which stability is guaranteed in the four listed classes. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem about stability thresholds for GKK and τ-matrix classes.

status_evidence.title: Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable
status_evidence.snippet: Provides unstable examples of GKK τ-matrices, showing not every such matrix is positive stable.
status_evidence.claim: Unstable GKK τ-matrices exist, so the threshold is finite, but the precise maximum n is not pinned down.
